summary: The paper proposes DIRECTER, an activation steering method that dynamically modulates steering strength via a plausibility-guided decoding loop combined with an attention-sensitivity-based layer ranking. The method is well-motivated, addresses a real problem (oversteering) in existing attention steering baselines like PASTA and SpotLight, and shows consistent improvements on IFEval, LIFBench, and a new GSM8K-Format benchmark across model families (Llama 3.1/3.2, Qwen-2.5) and scales (1B–14B). The empirical evidence is reasonably thorough with sensible ablations (fixed-strength variants, reversed/random ranking, random-token control), robustness sweeps over β and α, and efficiency/quality analyses, though statistical reporting is thin and the theoretical grounding of the sensitivity metric is admittedly informal.
strengths: Addresses a concrete and recognized failure mode (oversteering) with an intuitive, decoding-time adaptive mechanism, rather than yet another static steering vector.

Combines two orthogonal ideas — plausibility-gated rejection of steered predictions and sensitivity-ranked layer selection — with the gating shown to be a general-purpose safety filter that also improves PASTA and SpotLight (Fig. 2b).

Broad empirical coverage: multiple benchmarks (IFEval, LIFBench, GSM8K-Format), multiple model families and scales (1B–14B), tuned rather than only default baselines, LLM-judged and human-evaluated text quality/task fidelity, and inference efficiency measurements.
Sensible ablations isolating each design decision: reversed ranking, random layers, random tokens, fixed-strength variants (ST1–ST6), β and α sweeps, and prompt-format robustness.
Efficiency profile is practical: ~16% throughput drop with negligible memory overhead and compatibility with FlashAttention, unlike attention-logit-biasing baselines.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical soundness is thin: results are reported with greedy decoding and, for most cells, no seeds/error bars/significance tests. Only two ablation rows (random layers, random tokens) show ±std. Gains such as 61.6 vs 61.3 (Llama-3.2-1B) or 74.4 vs 74.9 (Qwen-7B) in Table 2 are within plausible noise without variance estimates.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds/prompt permutations (or nonzero-temperature runs) for at least the main tables, and add a paired significance test on IFEval and GSM8K-Format between DIRECTER and the strongest tuned baseline.

key_concerns.issue: Fairness of the hyperparameter protocol needs clarification. Baselines (PASTA*, SpotLight*) are 'tuned on IFEval' with a single setting reused; DIRECTER uses a fixed α=100, β=0.5 across tasks 'without task-specific tuning' but β=0.5 appears empirically optimal per Fig. 3a — i.e., it was still selected. Given greedy decoding and small gaps, this asymmetry could inflate the apparent margin.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State explicitly how β=0.5 and α=100 were chosen, apply the same selection protocol (best on IFEval, then transferred) uniformly to all methods, and ideally report a leave-one-benchmark-out tuning result.

key_concerns.issue: The attention-sensitivity metric is empirically justified but theoretically unmotivated, and the ablation only compares against reversed and random orderings. It is unclear whether simpler heuristics (e.g., layer index/depth prior, gradient- or activation-norm-based ranking, or the PASTA head-profiling reduced to layers) would match performance without the one-time forward-pass cost.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one non-random, non-reversed baseline ranking (e.g., top-k by attention entropy shift, gradient norm on the instruction span, or middle-layer heuristic) and report performance and cost.

key_concerns.issue: Some claims are mildly overstated: 'up to 6.5% over baselines' is an average delta vs zero-shot, but Tables 2/4 show gains often within ~1–2 points of the tuned baseline on individual settings; and 'matching the text quality of non-intervention baselines' rests on a single LLM-judge score (4.40 vs 4.39–4.43) without variance.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Scope headline numbers to what the tables show (e.g., 'up to +X on IFEval; average +Y over tuned steering baselines') and add variance for the text-quality/task-fidelity judgments.

key_concerns.issue: The extraction shows several truncations/typos in Algorithm 1 (missing lines around lines 6/12) and in equations (e.g., the D_j formula splits terms in an unclear way, and the softmax argument reads 'S(l) = Q(l)(K(l))/d' without the transpose or sqrt visible). Even allowing for anonymization artifacts, the current body text of Algorithm 1 as printed is not self-contained.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Re-render Algorithm 1 and equations (2)–(3) cleanly, ensuring that all conditional branches, the plausibility check line, and the disturbance-score decomposition are readable in the main text.

key_concerns.issue: Related work discusses activation steering primarily via PASTA/SpotLight and contrastive-vector methods, but does not position DIRECTER against decoding-time contrastive/plausibility methods it cites (DoLa, contrastive decoding) or against recent adaptive-strength steering work; the delineation is qualitative rather than empirical.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least a brief empirical or conceptual comparison against a contrastive/plausibility decoding baseline (e.g., DoLa) and a recent adaptive-strength steering method to justify the specific coupling proposed here.

questions_for_authors: How were α=100 and β=0.5 selected, and does DIRECTER retain its lead under the same selection protocol you apply to PASTA*/SpotLight* (best on IFEval, held fixed elsewhere)?
Can you provide seed-level variance and paired significance tests on IFEval, LIFBench, and GSM8K-Format, particularly for the close cells in Table 2 (e.g., Qwen-7B and 14B)?
How sensitive is DIRECTER to the halving schedule for |L_cand|? Would other reduction schedules (linear, geometric with different ratios) change the accuracy/throughput trade-off?
How does the sensitivity ranking compare against cheaper heuristics (depth prior, attention-entropy shift, gradient-norm)? Is the one-time analysis cost justified relative to a simple heuristic?

In the gating rule p_{t,i_t^{(2)}} < β · p_{t,i_t^{(1)}}, what fraction of decoding steps trigger a steered forward pass in practice on each benchmark, and how does this correlate with the accuracy gains?
For the 'automatic span detection' setting mentioned in the limitations, how does DIRECTER's advantage change when instruction/task tokens are not cleanly separable?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly scoped to the evidence, but the headline '6.5% improvement' and 'matches non-intervention text quality' would benefit from tighter wording and variance estimates; other statements (efficiency, oversteering mitigation as a general mechanism) are well supported by the presented ablations.

significance.justification: Instruction-following via inference-time steering is an active area, and a robust adaptive mechanism that mitigates oversteering — and generalizes as a filter for other methods — is a useful contribution that ICLR readers would build on.

novelty.justification: The individual ingredients (KV cache scaling, plausibility/contrastive decoding, sensitivity-based layer selection) are known, but their coupling into a dynamic, per-step rejection loop over sensitivity-ranked layers is a genuinely new combination with a clear motivation.

rigor.justification: Method is clearly derived and the ablations plausibly isolate each design choice, but the sensitivity metric is admittedly heuristic and some baselines' hyperparameter protocols are not fully symmetric with DIRECTER's.

statistical_soundness.justification: Greedy decoding with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests on the main tables; only two ablation cells carry ±std, making several close comparisons hard to trust.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (theoretical grounding, span separability) are acknowledged, but the abstract's '6.5% over baselines' and text-quality parity claims are somewhat overreached given single-run point estimates.

clarity.justification: Overall structure and motivation are clear, but Algorithm 1 and equations (2)–(3) in the provided text are garbled/truncated in places, and some notation (H^{(l)}_pre/post, disturbance decomposition) is dense on first reading.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard Abstract–Intro–Related–Method–Experiments–Conclusion structure with limitations, appendices, and RQ-guided experimental section; length appears within ICLR norms.

reproducibility.justification: Models, benchmarks, key hyperparameters (α, β), decoding strategy, and baseline tuning are specified; however, seed policy, exact ranking algorithm details in the main text, and GSM8K-Format construction are only partially described.

related_work.justification: Reasonable coverage of activation steering and instruction tuning, but positions primarily against PASTA/SpotLight and does not empirically or conceptually contrast with adaptive-strength steering or contrastive-decoding methods it cites.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative displays: overview schematic (Fig. 1), plausibility-guidance ablations (Fig. 2), robustness sweeps (Fig. 3), and efficiency (Fig. 4); tables clearly support the main claims.

breadth_generality.justification: Evaluation spans multiple benchmarks, two model families, and 1B–14B scales, and includes efficiency and quality/fidelity analyses; still, all models are ≤14B and all English instruction-following, so 'general mechanism' claims are moderately supported.

overall_recommendation.justification: A borderline-accept: solid, useful contribution with broad experiments, held back mainly by weak statistical reporting and some asymmetry in baseline tuning; fixable with a moderate revision.
